title: UDP: Fix conversations over UDP
description:
UDP Stream IDs aren't correct when a deinterlacing key is involved,
particularly conversations with ephemeral server ports aren't
tracked correctly. Undesirable side effects noticed on SNMP and
TFTP are corrected.

**Notes for the reviewer:**

The idea was to fix the SNMP dissector behavior, particularly the conversation tracking when a deinterlacing key is used, but that leads to more significant changes.

There seems to be an assumption that the UDP conversation is equivalent to the SNMP one, which is weird if the server is using ephemeral ports. For this reason, it looks necessary to break the 1:1 UDP-SNMP conversation relationship (technically, by explicit calls to conversation_set_dissector).

A new conversation search option NO_GREEDY is added, then it's possible to interrupt and return immediately when a particular option was looked for, even if no conversation is matching. This avoids the default fall-through conversation search algorithm which can bring an undesired result.
Together, this new option and breaking of 1:1 conversations relationship, seem to restore a consistent behavior at the packet list level for the conversation line (it takes the UDP conversation).

As there is no stream_id support at the SNMP level, there is no conversation line for SNMP, only for UDP. Testing on earlier versions of Wireshark shows nothing is changing for that point. However, we might add this later.

Probably some other protocols with server ephemeral ports would need a similar fix. For now, TFTP isn't one of them but it looked necessary to fix it for the deinterlacing compatibility.

This appears to have broken certain RTP conversations that are setup.

E.g., rtsp_sdp_in_DESCRIBE_reply_quicktime.pcap and rtsp_sdp_in_http_reply_quicktime.pcap from #5208 no longer call the conversation dissector that was set up with `conversation_set_dissector` after `rtp_add_address` was called, and end up calling by default the RDT dissector (which is set to that port by default). Prior to this commit, it correctly called the RTP dissector.

The problem is that some protocols with an SDP call [s]rtp_add_address with both ports (but only one address), e.g. RSTP and DTLS-SRTP, and thus can create a NO_ADDR2 (but *not* `NO_ADDR2|NO_PORT2`) conversation with a handle set to it, which neither your `NO_GREEDY` nor the `NO_PORT_B` `find_conversation` finds.

I see, we are in a different case where the suggested algo no longer works.
For now, it should be better to revert it while I'm trying to find a more general solution ?

Perhaps. I haven't fully looked at it all. It would work on these cases to check to call `revconvnob = find_conversation_strat(pinfo, CONVERSATION_UDP, 0, true);` instead of with `NO_PORT_B` (so it also searched `NO_ADDR_B`), but I don't know if the whole algorithm works.

The functions added for handling the _deinterlacing strategy_ have different signatures than their respective classical equivalents (in short: they're relying on `pinfo` instead of a bunch of arguments). As a consequence, they're unable to manage the non-ordinary cases, such as these ones over UDP involving multiple dissectors.

Fixing this (making that deinterlacing thing work in all cases) requires expanding the API by creating functions with the same signatures. At the end we could still keep the simple functions based on pinfo, as helper functions which are likely to be called most of the times (and more efficient as they have smaller signatures).

I'm then currently working on that.
I am preparing !19481 to fix all this mess.
@johnthacker !19481 looks finished to me, would you please take it into account ?

The DTLS-SRTP example in #13193 also now fails to call the RTP dissector (unless the heuristic RTP over UDP dissector is on; that doesn't help the RTSP example above because it's using a port registered to another protocol.)
